title: OKR Runway Harmonizer — Initiative Phasing, Risk Buckets, and Commitment Transfer Protocol
creator: Aisha Murthy
description:
Problem: As multiple company-level OKRs progress through the quarter, teams are repeatedly blocked by unclear initiative phasing, ad-hoc mid-cycle scope transfers, and inconsistent risk triage. This results in noisy escalation, duplicated work, and misaligned resource commitments.

Goal: Create a playbook and lightweight orchestration pattern (the 'OKR Runway Harmonizer') that standardizes: 1) initiative phasing (discover -> commit -> deliver -> sustain), 2) risk bucketing and escalation lanes, and 3) a Commitment Transfer Protocol for cross-team handoffs (when initiative ownership or effort shifts mid-cycle). The output should be a runnable process, templates, and a small console dashboard view to show initiative runway state.

Scope: Company-level OKRs and initiatives that span >1 team and affect Dedicated/Private product releases, Console features, or runtime infra behavior. Not in scope: purely single-team tactical chores or infra ops incidents (those follow incident runbooks).
acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc published in Confluence with clear step-by-step flows for phasing and transfer
A Commitment Transfer Protocol template (ownership transfer form) available and used by at least two cross-functional pilots
Console prototype tile that visualizes initiative phase and risk bucket for company OKRs (read-only)
Reduction in mid-cycle unplanned scope transfers for pilot initiatives by >=40% in the first 6 weeks
Stakeholders (PM, Eng, Design, Security, SRE) have signed off on escalation lanes and SLAs
proposed_solution: 1) Define a 4-state initiative model with explicit gates and artifacts required at each gate (e.g., PRD-lite, resourcing table, risk bucket, testing signoffs). 2) Introduce 'Risk Buckets' (None/Low/Medium/High) mapped to escalation lanes and approval needs. 3) Build a Commitment Transfer Protocol form (Google Form + Confluence template + Slack workflow) to record transfers, reasons, impact, and rollback plan. 4) Small Console read-only dashboard that pulls initiative metadata for visibility. 5) Pilot with two cross-functional initiatives (one infra/runtime, one Console feature) for a single cycle.
milestones: 2026-03-22: Alignment workshop with Eng Leads, Design, SRE, Security

risks: Process fatigue: teams may treat the playbook as additional bureaucracy rather than enabling clarity
Data freshness: Console tile may not reflect real-time changes without a small integration effort
Escalation overload: without tight SLAs, escalation lanes could create more meetings rather than fewer
Tooling friction: Commitment Transfer Protocol requires a light automation to avoid manual bookkeeping
metrics: Percent of company initiatives with a defined phase and completion date
Number of mid-cycle ad-hoc ownership transfers (baseline and change)
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Doc): Publish playbook & templates and gather feedback (2 weeks)
Phase 1 (Pilot): Apply to two initiatives and iterate on tooling (4 weeks)
Phase 2 (Tooling): Build small Console tile and Slack workflow to streamline transfers (4 weeks)
Phase 3 (Adoption): Encourage org-wide use for company-level OKRs and include in quarterly planning checklist
follow_up_tasks: Create Confluence page and embed Commitment Transfer Google Form
Coordinate alignment workshop with Eng leads and SRE
Open GH repo for Console prototype and assign ENG owner
Define SLAs for escalation lanes with Security and SRE
Schedule pilot retro and measurement plan
